data.title: Vision Blue Resources Secures Board Seat at USA Rare Earth with 7.9% Stake
data.description:
Vision Blue Resources Limited disclosed a 7.9% stake in USA Rare Earth, Inc. after receiving shares through the company’s merger with SVRE Holdings Ltd. on Sept. 3, 2026. The Schedule 13D, filed on Sept. 11, 2026, shows Vision Blue and its unit VB (Rare Earths) Limited now hold 29,544,227 common shares. The deal also gives the investor board representation tied to its ownership level.

Investor Intent

Vision Blue, through VB (Rare Earths) Limited, secured the right to appoint one director to USA Rare Earth’s board as long as it owns at least 5% of the company. "VBRE has the right to designate one member to the Issuer's Board," and the company named Sir Mick Davis to the seat at closing.

The investor can sell shares under a resale registration filed on Sept. 4, 2026, and accepted transfer limits under a lock-up: one-third of shares are freely tradable at closing, another third unlock after 90 days, and the rest after 180 days. The firm may buy more or sell shares in the future as it evaluates USA Rare Earth’s performance and other opportunities.

Investor's Background

Vision Blue Resources Limited is a Guernsey-based investment firm focused on strategic metals and minerals. The firm, founded by mining executive Sir Mick Davis, targets critical materials needed for the energy transition. Vision Blue typically partners with portfolio companies by providing growth capital and board-level guidance.

data.title: Stellantis Talks With Canadian Workers Hit Impasse on Plan to Sell Ontario Factory, Union Says — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Stellantis is in talks to sell its idled Toronto-area factory to a local defense firm, prompting the union representing over 9,000 of the automaker's Canadian employees to declare an impasse on talks toward a new labor deal.

The potential sale is the latest development involving the Stellantis factory in Brampton, Ontario, which hasn't operated since 2024 to undergo retooling.

Stellantis last year unveiled plans to shift the production of its next-generation Jeep Compass to Illinois from Brampton amid hefty Trump administration tariffs on foreign-made cars. The decision sparked the threat of a lawsuit from the Canadian government, which had provided Stellantis with hundreds of millions for work at the plants in Brampton and Windsor, Ontario.

Unifor, which represents auto-assembly workers, said Stellantis disclosed during talks on a new collective-bargaining agreement that the company had an interested buyer of the Brampton plant in a Canadian producer of smart-armored vehicles.

A Stellantis spokeswoman confirmed the interest from Canadian defense manufacturer Roshel, a maker of armored vehicles. Stellantis added that the two sides have signed a memorandum of understanding, which signals both companies' interest in pursuing a transaction.

"The persistence of the company's proposal to close and sell the Brampton plant has hindered the bargaining process," Unifor said, adding that talks have reached an impasse and are now paused. Unifor said the current labor deal expires on Aug. 20.

The Stellantis spokeswoman said Roshel represents the best option to restoring operations at its Brampton assembly plant, "preserving the site's strategic role in Canada's advanced manufacturing sector and helping to avoid a prolonged period of inactivity." She had no further comment, citing collective-bargaining talks with Unifor.

Representatives for Roshel didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. In interviews with Canadian media this summer, the company's chief executive, Roman Shimonov, said he was interested in the idle Brampton plant as the company required more factory space to meet demand.

"We know that many automotive companies pulled out from Canada, and that's exactly where defence can substitute and bring thousands of employees back, including in Brampton," Shimonov said at the time.

A spokeswoman for Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Government officials have been in talks about the future of the Brampton plant. Joly has threatened to launch a lawsuit against Stellantis, for failing to follow through with the Jeep Compass production, and vowed to recover the millions of dollars that governments provided to the car maker.

Trade relations between the U.S. and Canada have deteriorated in the past three weeks after talks unexpectedly collapsed toward a new trade pact, with both sides blaming the other for raising last-minute demands. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the negotiations with the U.S. revealed that the Trump administration wanted "to destroy our major industries, including our auto industry."

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: GE Vernova Stock Isn't All About Orders — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

Shares of power generation technology provider GE Vernova are a good example of the AI malaise settling over the market for financial reasons, such as peak AI spending by the hyperscalers, and social reasons, such as growing concerns about AI producing bad outcomes for humanity.

Wall Street rarely addresses the latter, but it often tackles the former. And an overemphasis on new spending has left GE Vernova stock at attractive levels, according to Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith.

Addressing "peak order myopia" in a Friday report, he pointed out that new building isn't all that drives GE Vernova's business.

GE Vernova's business is currently booming, with AI companies eager to secure power for their computers now and through the end of the decade. In the second quarter, equipment orders doubled year over year.

That's great, but investors will worry about everything. And fears that things were about as good as they can get hit the stock. Coming into Friday trading, Vernova shares were down more than 23% from a 52-week high of almost $1,196 reached near the end of June. Its drop corresponded with the fall in semiconductor stocks, another signal that investors are worried that AI spending has gone too far, too fast.

Peak spending might be a concern.

What GE Vernova stock doesn't reflect, however, is "peak services," says Dumoulin-Smith. Valuing GE Vernova based on 2029 and 2030 numbers missed the services opportunity. The company's service business will be half the size then that it will be in 2040.

"GE Vernova's earnings are inherently less sensitive to data center deployment fluctuations than competing portfolios exposed to inventory cycles such as low-voltage electrical equipment, energy management, and cooling," he says.

He rates shares Buy and raised his price target to $1,185 from $1,155. That values GE Vernova stock at about 45 times estimated earnings expected over the coming 12 months. Shares of electrical equipment providers Eaton and Schneider Electric are valued at closer to 30 times earnings, based on analysts' average price targets.

Dumoulin-Smith thinks the premium is warranted based on services. Large power-generating turbines need to be maintained and upgraded over time.

His peers appear to agree. Overall, 78% of analysts covering the company rate shares Buy, according to FactSet. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%. The average analyst price target for GE Vernova stock is about $1,240, higher than Dumoulin-Smith's.

The positive call might be helping. GE Vernova shares were up 3.1% in midday trading at $952.94, while the S&P 500 was up 1.1%.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@barrons.com.

data.title: 'Titanic' has a happy ending: Robust rally caps Wall Street's week of red
data.description:
Key points:
  • All three main US indexes end higher; Dow out front, up ~1%
  • Comm svcs lead S&P 500 sector gainers; just utilities and healthcare slip
  • Dollar ~flat; bitcoin, gold gain; US crude down ~2%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.97%

'TITANIC' HAS A HAPPY ENDING: ROBUST RALLY CAPS WALL STREET'S WEEK OF RED

U.S. stocks rebounded on Friday, snapping a four-session losing streak as investors shook off a could-have-been-worse inflation report and girded their loins for a near-term rate hike as they searched the carnage for bargains.

They found those bargains, apparently. All three major U.S. stock indexes ended sharply higher—just about 1% each—in a broad rally.

But the rally was too little and too late to salvage the week; all three indexes ended lower than last Friday's close.

Six of the "Magnificent Seven" group of AI-related megacaps, all but Nvidia , advanced, while Alphabet's and Amazon.com's magnificence was more apparent than the remaining four.

Airlines (.SPCOMAIR), chips , housing-related , (.SPCOMHOME), and retail (.SPXRT) were among the outperformers.

All of this falls in the wake of a largely in line (but still hot) CPI report that appeared to solidify the probability that the Federal Reserve will follow the European Central Bank's example by hiking interest rates at the conclusion of next week's policy meeting.

The odds of that happening are now at 86.5%, according to CME's FedWatch tool, up from 59.4% a week ago. Even so, many analysts believe Fed Chair Warsh is more likely to hold rates steady, kicking the rate-hike can down the road a bit.

Oil took a bit of a breather on its hike into the clouds. Front month WTI and Brent crude futures settled down 2.4% and 2.8%, respectively. But both remain above $100 per barrel. For the week WTI surged about 9%.

data.title: EXEL Stock Slides After FDA Adds Three Months To Cancer Drug Review — William Blair Sees More Swings In Near Term
data.description:
Key points:
  • The FDA will now decide on Exelixis’s new application by March 3, 2027.
  • A March decision would push a possible U.S. launch out of this year and into 2027. 
  • William Blair said it was “surprised” by the three-month delay but still sees a low chance of an outright rejection, because the combination showed a survival benefit in the main study group.

Shares of Exelixis (EXEL) fell 2% on Friday after the company said U.S. regulators added three months to the review of its next cancer drug, but William Blair still sees a low chance of an outright rejection.

The Food and Drug Administration told Exelixis on Thursday that it had extended the review of a new drug application for zanzalintinib plus Roche’s Tecentriq in patients whose colorectal cancer has spread, the company said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. The new target decision date is March 3, 2027. The old date was December 3, 2026. A March decision would push a possible U.S. launch out of this year and into 2027.

Why The Clock Moved

The FDA asked for more information and Exelixis sent updated safety and efficacy results, the company said. The agency treated that package as a major change to the application and extended its review period.

The FDA accepted Exelixis’s application in February for adults with metastatic colorectal cancer who had already received standard chemotherapy. Patients whose tumors lacked a common RAS mutation also had to have tried a separate targeted drug first.

The filing rests on STELLAR-303, a late-stage study that tested Exelixis’s oral drug with Tecentriq against Bayer’s Stivarga. In the full study population, patients on the combination lived longer.

Doubt remains because a second, pre-set test missed its mark. In June, Exelixis said patients without active liver tumors showed a similar trend but not a statistically clear survival win. Investors have worried the mixed result could slow the review, narrow the label, or invite extra questions. Friday’s filing did not say the new data requested by the FDA came from that subgroup.

Analyst Shrugs Off Rejection Risk

William Blair said it was “surprised” by the three-month delay but still sees a low chance of an outright rejection, because the combination showed a survival benefit in the main study group. The firm said the extra wait should not materially cut the drug’s long-term sales, though the stock may swing more in the near term. It kept an ‘Outperform’ rating.

Zanzalintinib is Exelixis’s bid for a second commercial franchise after Cabometyx, the cabozantinib tablet that still accounts for nearly all of the company’s product sales. Cabometyx is approved for kidney, liver, and neuroendocrine cancers and generated about $2.12 billion in U.S. net product revenue in 2025.

How Did EXEL Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around EXEL stock fell from ‘neutral’ to ‘bearish’ over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from ‘normal’ to ‘high’ levels.

“A delay is a delay nothing else,” a Stocktwits user said.

View this Stocktwits post

EXEL stock has gained 28% year-to-date.

data.title: Stellantis signs memorandum of understanding with Roshel for potential Canadian factory sale
data.description:
By Kalea Hall

Jeep maker Stellantis has signed a memorandum of understanding with Canadian armored vehicle maker Roshel, outlining a potential sale of its idled car factory near Toronto, the automaker said on Friday.

Stellantis said after considering several potential opportunities for the facility, the company "believes that Roshel represents a strong path to restoring sustainable operations at Brampton Assembly."

Roshel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Bloomberg News first reported the memorandum of understanding.

Stellantis is in contract negotiations with Unifor, a Canadian union representing Stellantis, General Motors and Ford auto workers, to replace a deal that expires September 20.

Unifor said it was at an impasse with Stellantis "following 10 days of intensive talks." The union said it has paused negotiations and is considering next steps.

The company has not disclosed plans for its other Canadian plants: the Windsor Assembly Plant and Etobicoke Casting Plant, the union said.

"Stellantis has offered only conditional agreement with the economic pattern settlement tied to the closing of Brampton, creating added complications for reaching a deal," the union said in a statement, referring to a wage settlement.

Last month, union leaders said Stellantis notified them it was considering closing and selling the Brampton plant.

Stellantis closed Brampton in 2023 for retooling. Stellantis paused that work in 2025 before moving future production of its Jeep Compass to a factory in Illinois, ​after U.S. President Donald Trump imposed tariffs on Canadian goods.

data.title: SlowMist details Liquid Network exploit, attacker mints 3,998 L-BTC in largest Bitcoin sidechain hack of 2026
data.description:
A single software bug in Blockstream's Elements codebase allowed an attacker to conjure nearly 4,000 unbacked L-BTC out of thin air, peg them out for real Bitcoin, and drain roughly 95% of the Liquid Federation's reserves in a matter of hours. SlowMist published its full analysis of the September 6 exploit on September 11, confirming what is now the largest publicly disclosed security incident involving a Bitcoin sidechain this year.

The damage: approximately 3,998.5 L-BTC minted and redeemed, worth roughly $320 million. The Liquid Federation's reserve wallet went from holding over 4,200 BTC to about 197 BTC.

The root cause, according to SlowMist's analysis, was a cache key collision vulnerability buried in the range-proof verification process. Range proofs are cryptographic checks that confirm transaction amounts fall within valid bounds without revealing exact values. They're fundamental to Liquid's confidential transaction model.

To speed up verification, Elements cached previously validated proofs so it wouldn't have to recheck them. The problem was how those cache keys were constructed. Prior to version v23.3.4, the software generated cache keys without length prefixes. Two different inputs could produce identical cache keys, meaning the system would treat an invalid proof as already verified if its key happened to collide with a legitimate one.

The attacker exploited this collision to bypass verification, minting L-BTC that had no corresponding Bitcoin backing in the federation's peg wallet. Those freshly minted tokens were then rapidly pegged out, converting them into real BTC on the Bitcoin mainnet before anyone could intervene.

Blockstream moved quickly after discovering the exploit. Peg operations were suspended, halting any further outflows. The network's block production itself was paused and didn't resume until September 10, after the team deployed Elements v23.3.4 with patched cache key management that includes proper length prefixes.

Blockstream confirmed that the incident was caused by a software bug, not a compromise of the federation's signing keys.

The attacker communicated via Bitcoin OP_RETURN messages, a method of embedding short text strings directly into Bitcoin transactions. The messages identified the attacker as a white-hat researcher and included a demand for a 10% bounty.

Roughly 3,400 BTC were returned to the federation peg wallet following the patch. The attacker retained approximately 598.5 BTC, presumably their self-assessed finder's fee. The math works out to about 15% of the total haul, not the 10% originally requested.

The vulnerability wasn't in the federation's governance or key management. It was in a performance optimization. Caching verified proofs is a perfectly reasonable thing to do. The implementation just happened to contain a flaw that turned a speed improvement into a $320 million attack vector.

The network was offline for four days. Ninety-five percent of its reserves vanished before anyone noticed. And the recovery depended, in part, on the attacker's willingness to return funds.

SlowMist's analysis specifically flags the absence of length prefixes in cache key construction as the enabling factor, a detail that other projects using similar patterns should audit immediately.

data.title: Rocket Lab Has Something SpaceX Doesn't. The Case to Buy the Stock. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

The space business is booming, and one of the best ways to play it is what some call the mini-SpaceX: space start-up Rocket Lab.

Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale launched coverage of Rocket Lab stock with a Buy rating and $80 price target, up about 30% from recent levels, on Friday.

Rocket Lab stock was up 0.8% in early trading at $62.64, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average were rising 1% and 1.2%, respectively.

Rocket Lab can launch rockets, assemble spacecraft, and is working on a larger rocket, Neutron, to boost capacity. In June, it announced plans to buy Iridium, giving Rocket Lab a satellite communications network, just like SpaceX.

"Upon closing Iridium, Rocket Lab will be the only vertically integrated space company with positive free cash flow and [a] partnership-led strategy that enables free cash flow to compound at a time when investment intensity declines," wrote Gesuale.

He projects positive free cash flow in 2028, which aligns with the Wall Street consensus. SpaceX isn't expected to have free cash flow until 2030. (It's spending a lot on AI data centers.)

"2028 provides the first clean view of the [business] model, with standalone Rocket Lab reaching about $1.8 billion revenue...and, pro forma for Iridium, [total revenue] increasing to about $2.9 billion," says Gesuale. Rocket Lab is expected to generate about $960 million in 2026 sales, up from roughly $600 million in 2025.

There is a lot of growth in space and space-based communications. It's a bold call that his peers largely agree with. Overall, 83% of analysts covering Rocket Lab stock rate shares Buy, according to FactSet. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%. The average analyst price target is about $112.

Wall Street loves the stock, but it's been dropping like, well, a satellite falling back to Earth. Coming into Friday trading, Rocket Lab stock was down 46% over the past three months. Nothing really bad happened. The company reported better-than-expected second-quarter sales in August and provided a solid outlook for the third quarter.

The problem was mainly SpaceX-or the hype surrounding it. Space-related stocks ran up into SpaceX's record-setting June IPO only to sell off after. Shares of Rocket Lab, which, like SpaceX, offers launch and satellite services, albeit at a smaller scale, traded north of $150 in late May. Shares closed below $59 in late July, a few weeks after the IPO, as SpaceX stock fell below its $135 IPO price.

SpaceX is important for the sector. It essentially created the modern space economy with its pioneering use of reusable rockets. And SpaceX's trillion-dollar valuation signals a major opportunity in space, on which other companies, including Rocket Lab, can capitalize.

data.title: S&P 500 ends higher as strong inflation data cements rate-hike bets
data.description:
Key points:
  • CPI up 0.4% in August, after 0.1% rise in July
  • Dell hits record high, hardware stocks climb
  • S&P 500 +0.86%, Nasdaq +0.96%, Dow +0.98%

By Noel Randewich

Wall Street ended higher on Friday as oil prices retreated and strong consumer price data reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to fight inflation.

AI server maker Dell soared 12% to a record high. Hewlett Packard Enterprise jumped 12% and HP gained 8.4% after Oracle's quarterly results topped estimates. Oracle dipped 1.8%.

U.S. consumer prices accelerated last month as the cost of gasoline rebounded after two straight monthly declines, adding pressure on the Fed to tighten monetary policy to fight inflation.

Interest rate futures now reflect a nearly 90% probability that the central bank will raise rates at its policy meeting on Wednesday, according to the CME FedWatch tool. That is up from a 72% likelihood on Thursday.

"That's pretty much as close to a slam dunk as you're going to get," said Thomas Martin, senior ⁠portfolio manager at GLOBALT Investments in Atlanta. "The Fed will do the right thing and raise rates, and that is good at the margin for keeping inflation in check."

The S&P 500 climbed 0.86% to end the session at 7,656.98 points.

The Nasdaq gained 0.96% to 26,333.04 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.98% to 52,573.29 points.

Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by communication services , up 1.35%, followed by a 1.13% gain in consumer discretionary .

Volume on U.S. exchanges was relatively light, with 14.0 billion shares traded, compared with an average of 14.9 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

The CBOE Volatility Index , Wall Street's fear gauge, fell 2 points to 15.88.

Friday's rally follows recent nervousness on Wall Street related to inflation and rising long-term Treasury yields, as well as concerns about massive spending to build AI data centers. The S&P 500 is down about 2% from its record-high close on August 13, and it remains up 12% in 2026.

For the week, the S&P 500 dipped 0.8% and the Nasdaq lost 0.7%.

The S&P 500's recent decline, coupled with a strong earnings outlook, has the benchmark trading at 19 times expected earnings. That is its cheapest since April 2025, when U.S. President Donald Trump's "Liberation Day" tariff announcements threw global markets into a tailspin.

Oil prices fell but remained up around 9% for the week as attacks along Middle East shipping routes stoked concerns about prolonged supply disruptions. Brent crude futures slipped almost 3% but were still above $104 a barrel.

Shares of ACV Auctions soared 44% after online vehicle auctioneer Copart agreed to buy it in a nearly $1.9 billion deal.

Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 2.1-to-one ratio.

The S&P 500 posted eight new highs and nine new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 45 new highs and 182 new lows.

data.title: TSX pares weekly decline as tech shares rally
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

Canada's main stock index clawed back some of its weekly decline on Friday, led by gains for technology shares, as a pullback in oil prices and the prospect of tighter U.S. monetary policy eased some concerns about the inflation outlook.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended up 191.21 points, or 0.5%, at 35,697.49, after hitting its lowest closing level in nearly six weeks on Thursday.

  • For the week, the index was down 2.2%, its fourth straight weekly decline and the steepest since March.

  • Wall Street also rallied on Friday as oil prices retreated and strong consumer price data reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to fight inflation.

  • "Equities enjoyed a small relief rally," Douglas Porter, chief economist at BMO Capital Markets, said in a note.

  • "In part, this reflected a modest late-week pullback in oil prices ... but it also may partly reflect the view that with the Fed now most likely to start tightening again, the medium-term outlook for inflation may be less fraught," Porter said.

  • U.S. crude oil futures settled 2.4% lower at $100.05 a barrel after a report that foreign ministers in the Middle East are trying to work out a temporary deal with Iran to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

  • The technology sector rose 3.6%, with shares of electronic equipment company Celestica gaining 6.6%.

  • Industrials (.GSPTTIN) added 0.7% and heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) ended 0.6% higher. The materials group , which includes metal mining shares, was up 1.1% as gold rallied.

  • Four of the 10 major sectors ended lower, including energy. It was down 0.7%.

data.title: LatAm stocks, FX fall as US rate hike bets weigh; Bolsonaro probe in focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • LatAm FX stocks down 1%, FX fall 0.4%
  • Brazilian consumer prices fall in August
  • Peru central bank holds rate at 4.25%
  • Mexico, Washington sprint toward bilateral trade deal before US elections

By Avinash P and Ragini Mathur

Latin American stocks and currencies fell on Friday amid fresh concerns over Brazil's presidential election outlook and mounting expectations of a U.S. interest-rate hike after stronger-than-expected inflation data.

MSCI's gauge of Latin American stocks (.MILA00000PUS) dropped 1% and was on track for its steepest weekly loss in a month.

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the leading right-wing challenger to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in next month's election, is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering linked to failed lender Banco Master, according to court documents unsealed on Friday.

The development weighed on Brazilian assets, after recent polls pointed to a close race between Bolsonaro and Lula. Markets view Bolsonaro as more business-friendly.

Brazil's benchmark equity index fell 0.8%, though it remained on track for a fourth consecutive weekly gain. The Brazilian real edged 0.3% lower and was little changed for the week.

INFLATION DATA

Separately, Brazil's annual inflation slowed more than expected in August as consumer prices posted their steepest monthly decline in four years, strengthening the case for the central bank to deliver another interest rate cut next week.

"The BRL is increasingly being driven by politics rather than monetary policy," said UBS analysts, in a note.

"While this shift in sentiment remains supportive, it has also compressed Brazil's risk premium, leaving the real more exposed to election-related headlines and polling volatility."

Closely watched U.S. CPI data showed inflation accelerated in August as the cost of gasoline rebounded after two straight monthly declines. The data bolstered expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates next week, pressuring emerging-market assets.

MSCI's LatAm FX index (.MILA00000CUS) was trading 0.4% lower and was little changed for the week.

Oil prices eased on Friday but remained north of $100 a barrel as the latest attacks along Middle East shipping routes stoked concerns about prolonged supply disruptions.

While net oil exporting countries in the region have benefited from higher crude prices, fears persisted that prolonged inflation could complicate central-bank policy globally.

US-MEXICO TALKS, PERU RATE DECISION IN FOCUS

Mexico and the U.S. are working to secure a bilateral trade deal before the U.S. midterm elections in less than eight weeks, according to six sources familiar with the talks. The effort has gained urgency following the collapse of Canada's negotiations with Washington.

The Mexican stocks benchmark index dropped 0.3%. The peso added 0.1%.

Peru's central bank held its benchmark interest rate at 4.25% on Thursday, extending its pause for a 12th straight meeting, in line with market expectations.

The sol fell 0.1%, while stocks in Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) edged 0.2% lower.

Also on Thursday, data showed Argentina's monthly inflation slowed to 1.7% in August, as easing food-price pressures extended a run of lower readings under libertarian President Javier Milei.

Argentine stocks fell 1.9%, while the peso rose 0.3%.

data.title: Grades fall as US adds more rigs, supply concerns ease over potential Hormuz talks
data.description:
Grades fell on Friday, dealers said, as an increase in U.S. drilling activity and signs of potential progress in talks over Strait of Hormuz shipping eased supply concerns.

A closely watched report released by Baker Hughes on Friday showed that oil rigs, an early indicator of future output, rose by one to 450 this week.

Separately, a Financial Times report on Friday said foreign ministers of Gulf countries plan to meet their Iranian counterpart in a push by Oman and Iran to secure buy-in for a temporary deal to manage shipping through the strait.

Keeping a floor on prices, however, were fears of further disruptions to Middle East oil flows and global oil inventories. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Friday, tightening their grip on the vital global shipping route in the Iran war.

Global oil supply and demand look set to fall further than previously expected this year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, due to the war, with world supply in 2026 now expected to decline by 5.7 million barrels per day, or about 6%.

Oil and gas producer Chevron's CEO Mike Wirth said on Friday that oil buffers that limited crude price increases earlier in the Iran war have been depleted, and the conflict could lift prices further over the next few months.
